title: Career Roadmap: Policy Analyst
summary: A Policy Analyst researches public issues, evaluates government programmes, examines legislation, and develops evidence-based recommendations to improve policies and public services. Policy Analysts help governments, think tanks, nonprofits, research institutions, and businesses understand the likely effects of policy decisions.

facts.Current degree: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies (BA / B.Sc Liberal Arts & Sciences)

blocks.text: A Policy Analyst researches public issues, evaluates government programmes, examines legislation, and develops evidence-based recommendations to improve policies and public services. Policy Analysts help governments, think tanks, nonprofits, research institutions, and businesses understand the likely effects of policy decisions.

A Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies degree with a flexible major-minor structure can be a suitable foundation because policy analysis combines social sciences, economics, political science, research methods, statistics, and communication.

rows.text: Liberal Arts & Sciences with a relevant major-minor combination
Political Science, Economics, Public Policy, Sociology, Psychology, International Relations
Statistics, Data Science, Law, Economics, Research Methods, Communication
Policy research, critical thinking, data analysis, report writing
Government departments, think tanks, nonprofits, consulting firms, international development organisations
MA in Public Policy, Public Administration, Economics, Development Studies, or related fields

blocks.label: Qualification note
blocks.text: Liberal Arts is a broad pathway rather than a specialised policy qualification. Students should deliberately select subjects that develop research, quantitative analysis, governance, and policy-writing skills. Some advanced policy research and specialist roles prefer a relevant master's degree.

sections.heading: What does a Policy Analyst do?

items.text: Research public problems such as education, healthcare, employment, poverty, climate change, and urban development.
Examine existing policies, legislation, budgets, and government programmes.
Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative data.
Evaluate whether policies achieve their intended outcomes.
Compare policy alternatives, costs, benefits, risks, and implementation challenges.
Interview stakeholders and consult research reports, surveys, and official datasets.
Prepare policy briefs, evidence reviews, presentations, and recommendations.
Monitor changes in regulations and public programmes.
Communicate findings to policymakers, organisational leaders, and the public.
Track policy implementation and recommend improvements.

blocks.text: Public Policy Analyst
Examines government policies, administrative decisions, public spending, and service delivery.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: governance, policy research, programme evaluation, policy writing
Education Policy Analyst
Studies educational access, learning outcomes, teacher development, curriculum reforms, and education financing.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: education research, survey analysis, programme monitoring, stakeholder engagement
Health Policy Analyst
Researches healthcare access, health financing, public health programmes, and service delivery.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: health systems, programme evaluation, statistics, health economics fundamentals
Social and Development Policy Analyst
Examines poverty, inequality, employment, gender, housing, social protection, and community development.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: sociology, field research, impact evaluation, qualitative methods
International Relations and Foreign Policy Analyst
Studies international agreements, diplomacy, geopolitical developments, trade policy, and security issues.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: international relations, geopolitical research, analytical writing, regional expertise
Environmental and Climate Policy Analyst
Evaluates environmental regulations, climate strategies, energy transitions, and sustainability programmes.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: environmental policy, sustainability, data interpretation, impact assessment

blocks.text: Year-by-year learning plan
Stage 1
Humanities and social science foundations

items.text: Study political science, economics, sociology, or related introductory subjects.
Learn how government institutions and public programmes operate.
Develop critical reading and academic writing skills.
Follow a public issue and summarise the evidence behind it.
Learn spreadsheet fundamentals.

blocks.text: Stage 2
Research and analytical methods

items.text: Learn research design, surveys, interviews, and sampling.
Study introductory statistics and data visualisation.
Practise evaluating the quality and limitations of sources.
Analyse an official dataset relevant to a public issue.
Write a structured research report with citations.

blocks.text: Stage 3
Policy evaluation and specialisation

items.text: Select a policy area such as education, health, employment, or climate.
Study programme evaluation and policy implementation.
Compare policy alternatives and assess their trade-offs.
Conduct a supervised research project or field study.
Prepare a policy brief with evidence-based recommendations.

blocks.text: Stage 4
Internships and career preparation

items.text: Apply for research, governance, or public policy internships.
Build a portfolio of policy briefs, data analyses, and research reports.
Learn basic data analysis using Excel and one additional tool.
Practise writing concise recommendations for non-specialist audiences.
Explore postgraduate programmes if required for the target role.

blocks.text: Adapt the stages to the actual duration and curriculum of the Liberal Arts programme.

rows.text: R, Python, SPSS, Stata where relevant
Power BI, Tableau, Python visualisation libraries
Google Scholar, university libraries, policy research repositories
Suitable survey tools and structured questionnaires

blocks.text: A beginner should prioritise research methods, Excel, clear writing, and source evaluation. More advanced statistical tools become valuable when the role involves quantitative impact evaluation or large datasets.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Public policy brief
Select a policy issue, explain the problem, review the evidence, compare possible interventions, and provide a concise recommendation.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: research, critical analysis, policy writing, evidence synthesis

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Government programme data analysis
Analyse publicly available data on a programme's coverage, expenditure, or outcomes. Identify trends and clearly explain what the data cannot establish.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Excel, statistics, data visualisation, policy interpretation

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Policy implementation assessment
Develop an evaluation framework for a public service programme, including objectives, indicators, data sources, and possible implementation risks.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: programme evaluation, indicator design, governance, monitoring

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Community needs assessment
Design a small, ethical survey or interview study about a local public issue, subject to appropriate supervision and consent.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: survey design, qualitative analysis, ethics, stakeholder engagement

For each project, include the policy question, background evidence, sources, method, findings, limitations, and recommendations. Clearly separate established facts from interpretations and proposed actions.

blocks.text: Preparation tracker
0 of 8 complete
Choose a policy-relevant major and complementary minor
Understand governance and core social science concepts
Learn research methods and basic statistics
Analyse a public dataset or programme
Write at least one evidence-based policy brief
Build a portfolio of research reports and analytical work
Complete a policy or research internship
Check postgraduate requirements for target specialist roles
By graduation, a competitive candidate should aim to have:

items.text: A strong foundation in at least one policy-relevant social science.
Practical skills in research methods, statistics, and evidence evaluation.
Two or three high-quality writing samples or policy projects.
Experience analysing official datasets or evaluating a programme.
The ability to communicate complex findings clearly and objectively.
Internship or supervised research experience.
A defined policy specialisation and a plan for further study where needed.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Liberal Arts & Sciences can be a suitable pathway to Policy Analyst roles when students deliberately combine a relevant major with research methods, statistics, and strong writing skills. For better employability, build a portfolio of evidence-based policy briefs and data-driven projects, and pursue internships with think tanks, research centres, public institutions, or social impact organisations. A master's degree in public policy or a related discipline can be valuable for more specialised or senior roles.
